Deal with any abnormalities promptly. 2. Tool magazine faults. The main faults of the tool magazine include the magazine not rotating or not reaching the proper position, the tool sleeve failing to clamp the tool, and the tool sleeve failing to move up or down completely. ① Tool magazine cannot rotate or does not reach the proper position. Reasons for the magazine failing to rotate might include: a loose coupling between the motor shaft and the worm shaft; a frequency converter fault (check whether its input/output voltages are normal); no control output from the PLC (possibly a relay failure in the interface board); mechanical connections being too tight; or the grid voltage being too low. Reasons for the magazine not reaching its position might include motor rotation faults or transmission mechanism errors. ② Tool sleeve cannot clamp the tool. The reason might be that the adjusting screw on the tool sleeve is loose or the spring is too loose, resulting in insufficient clamping force; or the tool is overweight. ③ Tool sleeve fails to move up or down completely. The reason might be improper adjustment of the device or excessive machining errors causing an incorrect shift fork position; or a limit switch is installed incorrectly or adjusted improperly, resulting in erroneous feedback signals. ④ If a tool sleeve cannot be disassembled or requires a waiting period before disassembly, check whether the cylinder and air valve that operate the tool sleeve's 90-degree up/down movement are loose, whether the air pressure is sufficient, and whether the rotary shaft of the tool sleeve is rusted. 3. Tool changing manipulator faults. ① Tool cannot be clamped tightly. Possible reasons include insufficient air compressor pressure, pressure booster leakage, tool clamping cylinder leakage, or the nut on the tool release spring being loose. ② Tool cannot be released after clamping. The possible reason is that the tool lock/release spring is compressed too tightly. Adjust the screw on the lock/release spring so that the maximum load does not exceed the rated value. ③ Tool falls out of the manipulator. Check whether the tool is overweight and whether the manipulator's clamping lock is damaged or has not sprung out. ④ Tool drops during tool exchange. During a tool change, if the spindle box does not return to the tool change point or the change point drifts, or if the manipulator starts pulling the tool before reaching the proper grasping position, a tool drop will occur. In this case, re-operate the spindle box movement to return it to the tool change position and reset the tool change point. ⑤ The manipulator's tool change speed is too fast or too slow. Possible reasons include air pressure being too high or too low, or the throttle opening of the tool change air valve being too large or too small. Adjust the air pressure and the throttle valve opening accordingly. 8.5.3 Common Fault Maintenance of Automatic Tool Changers. This type of bearing achieves preloading by causing axial displacement between the inner and outer rings under the action of axial force Fa0, as shown in Figure 9-6c. What measures the preload is the axial preload force Fa0, referred to as preload force, with the unit of N. Multi-unit angular contact ball bearings are assembled based on preload force; bearing factories specify three levels of preload: light, medium, and heavy, and the preload level can be specified when ordering. Based on the preload force, the bearing factory grinds away an amount σ from the end face of the inner ring (for back-to-back assembly, as shown in Figure 9-6d) or the outer ring (for face-to-face assembly, as shown in Figure 9-6e). When pressed tightly during assembly, the predetermined preload force can be obtained. If a certain distance is required between two bearings, inner and outer spacers of the same thickness can be added between the two bearings. Under the action of axial load, the rolling elements and the raceway of the unloaded side bearing must not separate from contact. The minimum preload force meeting this condition is 35% of the maximum axial load for a duplex configuration (approximately taken as 1/3), and 24% for a triplex configuration (approximately taken as 1/4). 3) Lubrication and sealing of spindle bearings. Good lubrication can reduce the operating temperature of bearings and prolong service life. Sealing not only prevents dust, chips, and cutting fluid from entering, but also prevents the leakage of lubricating oil. ① Lubrication of spindle bearings. On CNC machine tools, spindle bearing lubrication methods include grease lubrication, oil lubrication, oil mist lubrication, and oil-air lubrication. Grease lubrication is currently the most commonly used lubrication method for spindle bearings on CNC machine tools, especially for front support bearings. Of course, if there is no cooling lubricating oil system in the spindle box, the rear support bearings and other bearings generally use grease lubrication. The grease filling amount for spindle bearings is usually 10% of the bearing's spatial volume, and must not be filled arbitrarily, otherwise it will exacerbate spindle heating. When using grease lubrication, effective sealing measures must be taken to prevent cutting fluid or lubricating oil from entering the bearing. Oil lubrication is also one of the common lubrication methods in CNC. Figure 8-7 shows a constant temperature oil lubrication and cooling method. Constant temperature oil controlled by an automatic oil temperature control box enters the spindle box via a hydraulic pump, flows along the spiral groove on the outer ring of the spindle front support sleeve to take away the heat generated by the spindle bearing; another path injects constant temperature oil onto the transmission gears and transmission shaft support bearings via an oil distributor in the spindle box to take away the heat they generate. When using oil lubrication for angular contact ball bearings, attention should be paid to the pumping effect of angular contact, and oil needs to be injected from the small opening of the bearing. Oil mist lubrication is a method where oil is atomized by high-pressure gas and sprayed from a nozzle onto the parts requiring lubrication. Because it is mist-like, the oil has good heat absorption and no oil stirring effect, so it is often used for the lubrication of high-speed spindle bearings. However, oil mist is easily blown out and pollutes the environment. Oil-air lubrication is a new lubrication method developed for high-speed spindles. As shown in Figure 8-8, it feeds a very small amount of oil (8~16 min, about 0.03 cm³) into compressed air, and then blows it into the bearing clearance, thereby lubricating the bearing and suppressing bearing heat. The oil level switch in the oil tank and the pressure switch in the pipeline can automatically cut off the power supply of the main motor when there is no oil in the tank or insufficient pressure. ② Sealing of the spindle. Spindle sealing includes contact sealing and non-contact sealing. Figure 8-9 shows several forms of non-contact sealing. Figure 8-9a utilizes the clearance between the bearing cover and the shaft for sealing; grooving inside the bearing cover hole is to improve the sealing effect. This seal is used in grease-lubricated areas

(6) Protection and Lubrication of Ball Screw Pairs 1) Protection of ball screw pairs Like other rolling friction transmission devices, the ball screw pair should avoid the entry of hard dust or chip dirt, so a protective device must be installed. If the ball screw pair is exposed on the machine tool, a closed protective cover should be used, such as a spiral spring steel strip sleeve, a telescopic sleeve, and a folding sleeve. During installation, one end of the protective cover is connected to the side of the ball nut, and the other end is fixed to the support housing of the ball screw. If the ball screw pair is in a hidden position, sealing rings can be used for protection. Sealing rings are installed at both ends of the nut. The contact elastic sealing ring is made of oil-resistant rubber or nylon, and its inner hole is shaped to match the screw thread raceway; the contact sealing ring has a good dust-proof effect, but due to contact pressure, the friction torque slightly increases. The non-contact sealing ring, also known as a labyrinth sealing ring, is made of hard plastic. The shape of its inner hole is opposite to the screw thread raceway, with a slight gap, which avoids friction torque but has a poor dust-proof effect. Avoid hitting the protective device during work. If the protective device is damaged, it should be replaced in time. 2) Lubrication of ball screw pairs Lubricants can improve wear resistance and transmission efficiency, and are divided into two main categories: lubricating oils and lubricating greases. Lubricating oil is generally oil for total loss systems, and lithium-based grease can be used as lubricating grease. Lubricating grease is generally added to the thread raceway and the housing space where the nut is installed, while lubricating oil is injected into the nut space through the oil hole on the housing. The lubricating grease on the ball screw should be replaced every six months. Clean the old grease on the screw and apply new grease. Because the hydrostatic worm-rack drive has both the characteristics of pure liquid friction and the characteristics of the worm-rack mechanical structure, it is particularly suitable for the feed drive systems of heavy machine tools. Its main features are: ① Small frictional resistance. 8.3 Common Fault Analysis of Guideways. The quality of guideways has a great impact on the rigidity, machining accuracy, and service life of machine tools. As an important part of the machine tool feed system, CNC machine tools have higher requirements for guideways than ordinary machine tools. The basic requirements for guideways are as follows: ① High guiding accuracy. Guiding accuracy mainly refers to the straightness or roundness of moving parts when moving along the guideway. The main factors affecting guiding accuracy include the geometric accuracy of the guideway, contact accuracy of the guideway, structural form of the guideway, rigidity and thermal deformation of the moving and supporting guideways, assembly quality, and the stiffness of the oil film between hydrodynamic and hydrostatic guideways. ② Sufficient rigidity. Guideway rigidity refers to the ability of the guideway to resist deformation under dynamic and static loads. The guideway must have sufficient rigidity to ensure that it does not undergo excessive deformation under static loads, thereby ensuring the relative position and guiding accuracy between various components. ③ Good friction characteristics. The long-term operation of the moving guideway along the supporting guideway surface will cause uneven wear, destroy the guiding accuracy of the guideway, and thus affect the machining accuracy of the machine tool. The wear forms of guideways include abrasive wear, galling and thermal welding, fatigue, and crushing. ④ Smoothness of low-speed movement. When moving at low speeds, the moving guideway, acting as a moving component, is prone to stick-slip (crawling) phenomena. The stick-slip of feed motion will reduce workpiece accuracy, so it is required that the guideway moves smoothly at low speeds without stick-slip, which is especially important for high-precision machine tools. ⑤ Good damping characteristics (no vibration at high speeds). ⑥ Good structural manufacturability. 8.3.1 Structural Characteristics and Adjustment of Guideways. Currently, the guideways used in CNC machine tools are mainly of three types: sliding guideways, rolling guideways, and hydrostatic guideways. 1. Sliding Guideways. (1) Types of sliding guideways. The magnitude of rigidity, ease of manufacturing, adjustability, minimization of friction loss, and the ability to maintain initial precision of sliding guideways largely depend on their cross-sectional shapes (as shown in Figure 8-37). 1) Inverted-V (mountain-shaped) and V-shaped cross-sections. As shown in Figure 8-37a, this type of cross-section has high guiding accuracy, and after wear, it automatically compensates by sinking under its own weight. A convex lower guideway is conducive to discharging dirt but does not easily retain oil, often used in lathes; a concave lower guideway is the opposite, often used in grinders with a top angle generally at 90°. 2) Rectangular cross-sections. As shown in Figure 8-37b, this type is convenient to manufacture and repair, has a large load-bearing capacity, and new guideways have high guiding accuracy. However, it cannot automatically compensate after wear and requires gib adjustment, which affects guiding accuracy. 3) Cylindrical cross-sections. As shown in Figure 8-37c, this type is easy to manufacture and can achieve precision fits, but it is highly sensitive to temperature changes, easily jamming when clearances are small, and having poor guiding accuracy when clearances are large. Compared to the other cross-sections, it is less commonly used. 4) Flat annular cross-sections. As shown in Figure 8-37d, this type is suitable for rotary motion, easy to manufacture, and can withstand large axial forces, but guiding accuracy is relatively poor. Switching to a conical annular cross-section (Figure 8-37e) provides better guiding performance. 5) Dovetail cross-sections. As shown in Figure 8-37f, this type has a compact structure and can withstand overturning moments, but its rigidity is relatively poor, and manufacturing and maintenance are inconvenient. It is suitable for situations where guiding accuracy requirements are not excessively high. (2) Surface treatment of sliding guideways. The materials used for sliding guideways in CNC machine tools are cast iron attached with plastic or steel-inlaid attached with plastic. Commonly used guideway plastics include PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene) soft tapes and epoxy-based wear-resistant coatings. 1) Characteristics of PTFE guideway soft tapes: ① Good friction characteristics: The dynamic and static friction coefficients of the metal-PTFE soft tape are basically consistent. ② Good wear resistance: The PTFE soft tape material contains bronze, copper disulfide, and graphite, so it has self-lubricating properties and does not require high-quality lubricating oil. In addition, the plastic is soft, so even if metal chips and dust are embedded, it will not damage the metal guideway surface and the soft tape itself, prolonging the service life of the guideway pair. ③ Good vibration damping: The damping performance of plastic is good, resulting in effective vibration reduction and noise elimination, which helps improve movement speed. ④ Good manufacturability: It lowers the hardness and surface quality requirements for the metal substrate to which the plastic is bonded, and the plastic is easy to process (milling, planing, grinding, scraping), allowing the guideway pair contact surface to achieve excellent surface quality. Example 7: The spindle of an XK5040-1 could not rotate after starting up. Fault cause analysis and elimination: Checking the motor, the condition was good; the transmission key was not damaged. After adjusting the tension of the V-belt, the spindle still could not rotate. Checking the spindle electromagnetic brake, no problems were found with the armature's return spring or the friction disc. It was analyzed that it might be a damaged gear or bearing on the transmission shaft, causing the transmission to jam. Disassembling the transmission shaft, it was found that the bearing (EZ12) had burned out due to lack of lubrication. After removing it and turning the spindle by hand, it rotated normally. After installing a new bearing and testing, the spindle moved normally, but the spindle braking time was long. At this point, the clearance between the friction disc and the armature needed to be adjusted. First, loosen the lock nut, and then evenly adjust the four screws to move the armature upwards. After adjusting the clearance between the armature and the friction disc to 1mm, lock it with the nut and perform a test run. The spindle braked rapidly, and the fault was completely eliminated. Example 8: A machining center had poor spindle positioning, causing an interruption during the tool change process. Fault cause analysis and elimination: When this fault first appeared, the machine tool worked normally again after restarting, but subsequently, this fault appeared repeatedly. Carefully observing the machine tool, it was found that the fault was caused by a positional shift after the spindle was oriented. After the spindle was positioned, if touched by hand, the spindle would drift in the opposite direction. Checking the electrical unit, there were no alarms. According to the machine tool's manual, this machine tool uses an encoder for positioning; based on the fault phenomena and the possible parts involved, the likelihood of an electrical problem was relatively small. It was analyzed as a mechanical connection problem, so the connections of various parts of the spindle were inspected. When checking the encoder connection, it was found that the set screw on the encoder's connecting sleeve was loose, causing the connecting sleeve to retreat and resulting in excessive clearance in the connection with the spindle, making the rotation out of sync. After fixing the set screw according to the requirements, the fault was eliminated. Example 9: During the working process of a CNC milling machine, the mechanical variable-speed sliding gear in the spindle box automatically disengaged from meshing, and the spindle stopped rotating. Fault cause analysis and elimination: The variable-speed structure of this machine tool is a hydraulic shift fork variable-speed mechanism. The hydraulic cylinder pushes the sliding gear for speed variation and also locks the sliding gear. Therefore, the automatic disengagement of the shifting sliding gear is highly likely to be caused by pressure changes inside the hydraulic cylinder. Checking the hydraulic control oil circuit, it was found that the three-position four-way directional valve controlling the hydraulic cylinder was in the middle function position and could not seal completely. The oil circuits in the front and rear cavities of the hydraulic cylinder leaked into each other, causing the thrust in the upper cavity of the hydraulic cylinder to be greater than that in the lower cavity, causing the piston rod to move downwards gradually, gradually making the sliding gear disengage from meshing and causing the spindle to stop rotating. After replacing with a new three-position four-way directional valve, the fault was eliminated. Example 10: After a CNC milling machine issued a spindle box shifting command, the spindle entered a slow reciprocating swing state and could never engage the gear. Fault cause analysis and elimination: This machine tool adopts the hydraulic shift fork variable-speed mechanism shown in Figure 8-2 to achieve machine tool spindle speed variation. To ensure that the sliding gear smoothly meshes in the correct position, after the machine tool receives a shifting command, the electrical design instructs the main motor to drive the spindle to perform a slow reciprocating swing motion. Analysis indicated a fault in the solenoid valve (valve core stuck or solenoid failed), causing the oil circuit to be unable to switch, and the hydraulic cylinder did not act; or the hydraulic cylinder acted, but the contactless switch sending the feedback signal failed, and the feedback signal could not be sent after the sliding gear shifted into place, either of which would interrupt the machine tool's cycle action. After replacing the new hydraulic valve or the failed contactless switch, the fault was eliminated.

Example 3: Poor protection caused synchronous belt aging and deformation, resulting in feed deviation. Fault Cause Analysis and Elimination: During automatic operation of a CNC lathe, the actual machining size occasionally differed from the program-specified size when the X-axis was feeding, with a difference of about 0.5~2mm. Because this phenomenon occurred occasionally rather than continuously, and the CNC system did not display an alarm number when it occurred, the fault was very unclear. During work, operators could not guarantee whether the machining size of the next workpiece would be qualified, and scrap products continued to appear. First, the control system output signals were checked and found to be normal; then, after resetting the system, the X-axis feed speed was tested, and the data displayed by the system was consistent with the settings; after adjusting the system parameters and re-testing, the fault remained. Therefore, it was suspected that the speed of the X-axis drive stepper motor was unstable, and there might be a "missing step" phenomenon. Opening the protective cover of the X-axis drive stepper motor of the machine tool, the input phase voltage and speed of the motor were measured, and both were within normal ranges. Using an adjustable wrench to test-rotate the X-axis drive screw, it felt alternately tight and loose. Opening the screw cover, it was found that the synchronous timing belt connecting the stepper motor and the screw was severely aged, deformed, and even missing teeth. The reason was that the fastening screws of the protective cover at the connection part were loose, and cutting fluid seeped into the synchronous belt during machine operation. After soaking, it became severely aged and deformed, making it impossible for the stepper motor to synchronize with the screw speed, causing the above fault. After replacing the synchronous belt and re-running the test program, the command size was consistent with the actual measured size, and the fault was eliminated. Example 4: Coupling connection screws were loose, causing excessive position deviation in the feed direction. Fault Cause Analysis and Elimination: During the operation of a horizontal machining center, an alarm message indicating that the Y-axis position deviation exceeded the set value appeared. This machining center uses a FANUC 0iM system and adopts a closed-loop control format. Grating scales installed on the guide rail side and the column serve as position measurement components, and the system control takes the position loop as the outer loop; a rotary encoder installed at the end of the servo motor serves as the angle measurement component, and the speed loop is the inner loop of the system control. The servo motor and the ball screw are directly connected by a coupling. Based on the machine tool control principles and the machine tool transmission connection method, it was preliminarily judged that the cause of the alarm was a poor connection of the Y-axis coupling. A check of the Y-axis transmission system revealed that the coupling connection screws were loose. After tightening all the fastening screws in the Y-axis transmission system, the fault was eliminated. Example 5: System overload alarm. Fault Cause Analysis and Elimination: For the XH716 CNC vertical machining center, the system is a FANUC OM system. This machine tool frequently experienced overload alarms during machining, with alarm number 434, manifesting as excessive Z-axis motor current and motor heating. The alarm disappeared after stopping for about 40 minutes, but after resuming work for a while, the same type of alarm appeared again. After inspection and analysis, it was believed that the electrical servo system had no faults, and it was estimated that it was caused by the load being too heavy to pull. In order to distinguish whether it was an electrical fault or a mechanical fault, the Z-axis motor was removed and disconnected from the mechanism. When running again, the fault no longer occurred, thus confirming that it was caused by the mechanical screw or moving parts being too tight. After adjusting the anti-loosening nut of the Z-axis screw, the effect was not obvious. Later, the Z-axis guide rail taper jib was adjusted, the machine load was significantly reduced, and the fault was eliminated.

(3) Temperature Rise Problems 1) The influence of lubrication The choice of lubricating oil directly affects the temperature rise of the ball screw. Poor lubrication of the ball screw will produce a larger temperature rise, which may cause steel balls to crack or be damaged, thereby damaging the nut or screw ball grooves. Therefore, the timely replenishment of lubricating oil must be considered during the design process. If an automatic lubrication system cannot be used, the replenishment cycle of lubricating oil (grease) must be included in the maintenance manual. Generally, it is recommended to use bearing lubricating oil for ball screw oil lubrication, and lithium-soap-based grease for grease lubrication. The viscosity of the oil should be selected based on operating speed, working temperature, and load conditions. For high speed and low load conditions, it is best to use low viscosity oil; for low speed and high load, high viscosity oil is recommended. When applied in high-speed, heavy-load situations, forced cooling must be used to lower the temperature, and hollow screws should be used to introduce cooling oil to achieve the cooling effect. 2) The influence of pre-tension Generally, ball screws require certain pre-tension to achieve the purposes of improving accuracy and rigidity, but applying pre-tensioning force to the nut will increase the friction torque and resistance of the raceway, raising the temperature during work. It is recommended that the pre-tension should not exceed 8% of the screw's dynamic load. 3) The influence of pre-stretching When the temperature of the ball screw rises, the thermal stress effect will cause a slight elongation of the screw, so the length of the screw becomes unstable. In order to ensure the transmission accuracy and working stability of the feed drive system of CNC machine tools, the following requirements should be noted when designing the mechanical transmission device: ① Improve transmission accuracy and rigidity. The accuracy of the CNC machine tool itself, especially the transmission accuracy and positioning accuracy of the feed drive device, plays a key role in the machining accuracy of parts and is a characteristic indicator of CNC machine tools. Therefore, it is first necessary to ensure the machining accuracy of each transmission part, especially to improve the transmission accuracy of the ball screw and nut pair (linear feed system) and worm gear pair (circular feed system). In addition, adding reduction gears to the feed transmission chain to reduce the pulse equivalent (i.e., the distance the worktable moves when the servo system receives one command pulse) can also improve transmission accuracy from a system design perspective; transmission accuracy and rigidity can also be improved by pre-tensioning the transmission ball screw to eliminate the clearance of transmission parts such as gears and worm gears. ② Reduce the inertia of moving parts. The inertia of transmission parts affects both the starting and braking characteristics of the feed drive system, especially for parts running at high speeds, where the influence of inertia is even greater. Under the premise of satisfying transmission strength and rigidity, the mass of the actuating components should be minimized as much as possible, and the diameter and mass of rotating parts should be reduced to decrease the inertia of moving parts. ③ Reduce the frictional resistance of moving parts. The frictional resistance of the mechanical transmission structure mainly comes from the lead screw nut pair and the guide rails. In the feed drive system of CNC machine tools, to reduce frictional resistance, eliminate low-speed feed crawling, and improve the stability of the entire servo feed system, ball screws, rolling guides, plastic guides, and hydrostatic guides are widely used. ④ Fast response speed. The so-called fast response characteristic refers to the response speed of the feed drive system to input command signals and how quickly the transient process ends. Fast response is a dynamic performance of the servo feed system and reflects the tracking accuracy of the system. During the workpiece machining process, the worktable should be able to sensitively and accurately track instructions within the specified speed range, without missing steps or taking extra steps during operation. The response speed of the feed drive system not only affects the machining efficiency of the machine tool but also affects the machining accuracy. In the design, the rigidity, clearance, friction, and moment of inertia of the machine tool worktable and transmission mechanism should be optimized to the best possible values to improve the fast response characteristics of the servo feed system. ⑤ Strong overload capacity. Because the motor frequently changes direction and the acceleration and deceleration are very fast, the motor may work under overload conditions. This requires the motor to have a strong overload capacity, generally requiring it to withstand an overload of 4 to 6 times for several minutes without damage. ⑥ Good stability and long service life. Stability is the most basic condition for the normal operation of the servo feed drive system, particularly that it must not crawl under low feed speeds and must be able to adapt to changes in external loads without resonance. Stability is related to the system's inertia, rigidity, damping, and gain. Properly selecting these parameters to achieve optimal working performance is the goal of servo feed system design. The service life of a servo feed drive system mainly refers to the length of time it can maintain the transmission accuracy and positioning accuracy of the CNC machine tool, that is, the ability of each transmission component to maintain its original manufacturing accuracy. Therefore, the materials, heat treatment methods, and processing technologies of each transmission component should be reasonably selected, and appropriate lubrication methods and protective measures should be adopted to extend its service life. ⑦ Convenient operation and maintenance. CNC machine tools are high-precision automatic control machine tools, mainly used for single-piece, small-to-medium batch, high-precision, and complex production and machining. CNC machine tools have a high utilization rate, so the structural design of the feed drive system should facilitate maintenance and care, minimizing the maintenance workload to improve the utilization rate of the machine tool. 8.2.1 Typical Structures of Feed Drive Components Common mechanical transmission devices include ball screw pairs, hydrostatic worm-rack drives, preloaded double gear-racks, and linear motors. 1. Instance 2: For the CNC machine in Instance 1, during the tool change process when the spindle moves up to the tool claw, there is a misalignment of the magazine tool claw, and a noticeable noise occurs when pulling/inserting the tool, as if it is jamming. Fault analysis and processing: Misalignment of the magazine tool claw indicates that the magazine zero point may have shifted, or there is clearance in the magazine transmission, or the weight of the tools in the magazine is unbalanced, causing it to lean to one side. Because the tool insertion and pulling are unsmooth, it is estimated that the magazine zero point has shifted. Unload all tools from the magazine, manually crank the spindle to near the second reference point of the Y-axis, and use a feeler gauge to measure the gap between the magazine tool claw and the spindle drive key, confirming the shift. Pushing and pulling the magazine by hand cannot utilize the gap to correct it. Adjust parameter 7508 until the gaps between the magazine tool claw and the spindle drive key are basically equal; after restarting, tool changes execute normally. Instance 3: A VMC-65A machining center, after six months of use, experienced loose spindle tool pulling without any alarm information. Fault analysis and processing: The reasons a spindle fails to pull a tool tightly include: deformed or damaged spindle pulling disc springs; the pulling cylinder action not fully completing; or a loose threaded connection between the pull stud and the tool holder collet. Upon inspection, it was found that the threaded connection between the pull stud and the tool holder collet was loose, causing the tool holder collet to rotate with tool insertion/extraction and retract by about 1.5mm. This machine's pull stud and tool holder collet had no anti-loosening locking measures. When inserting/pulling tools, if the tool center deviates slightly from the spindle taper hole center, eccentric friction occurs between the tool holder collet and the tool holder. Under the combined action of this friction and impact, the thread loosens over time, resulting in the spindle's failure to hold the tool. After locking the threaded connection between the spindle pull stud and the tool holder collet with thread-locking sealant and tightening the lock nut, the fault was eliminated. Instance 4: The tool change system of a CNC machine did not actuate when executing a tool change command; the manipulator arm stopped mid-stroke, and the CRT displayed an alarm number. Checking the manual revealed this alarm number indicated that the tool change system manipulator position detection switch signal was '0' and 'magazine tool change position error'. Fault analysis and processing: Based on the alarm content, it can be diagnosed that the fault occurred in both the tool exchange device and the tool magazine. Because the corresponding position detection switches sent no signals to the PLC input interface, the machine interrupted the tool change. Causes for the switch having no output signal could include inductive switch failure or hydraulic/mechanical issues preventing complete actions. First, use a thin iron sheet to induce the proximity switch in the magazine to rule out the possibility of the magazine's proximity switch failing. Next, check the 'arm extended' switch SQ21 and 'arm retracted' switch SQ22 in the tool change device's manipulator. Since the arm stopped mid-stroke, the output signals of both switches were '0'; testing showed both switches were normal. Manually actuating the 'arm retract' solenoid valve Y21 to return the manipulator to the 'arm retracted' position restored the machine to normal, indicating that the manually controlled solenoid valve could position the tool exchange device, thus ruling out hydraulic or mechanical resistance causing the incomplete action. From the above analysis, the PLC input signals were normal, and the output action execution was correct, so the problem lay within the PLC or improper operation. Observation during operation revealed that the interval between two tool changes was less than the PLC's required time, causing an error in the PLC program execution and leading to the fault.
